title: Fresh projective rigid-motion and disocclusion holdout for the frozen D12.7 adaptive local-risk gate

correction.reason: The reused typed-envelope encoders require their D12.1 machine-readable spec as an input, but the original D12.8 parent roster froze only the two encoder files.
onlyPermittedChanges: bind the unchanged D12.1 typed-envelope spec by URI and SHA-256
change the experiment identity and output roots to fresh C1 identities
replace the original pre-tool snapshot with this pre-formal correction snapshot
update embedded spec SHA-256 constants after this corrected spec is frozen

question: On unseen opaque multi-owner Blender 5.2 scenes containing real rigid object motion, camera parallax, bounds loss and disocclusion, can transform-aware structural rejection prevent invalid history reuse while the frozen D12.7 radius-2 plus local-risk rule preserves its absolute RGB headroom and preregistered coverage?
decisionRole: confirmatory generalization test of the unchanged D12.7 candidate beyond static inputs; no D12, D12.5, D12.6 or D12.7 verdict is revised

requirements: Every fixture ID, raster, camera trajectory, surface trajectory, analytic owner ID, pass index, transform, material coefficient and formal path is unseen in D10.1 and D12 through D12.7.
No prior EXR, adapted array, mask, consumer payload or per-pixel measurement may be a D12.8 measurement input.
The structural validity rule, risk formula, inclusive threshold, comparator role, gates and verdict mapping are frozen before any D12.8 formal tool or render output exists.
Repeat 1 is primary; repeat 2 is an exact source and consumer identity control.
A preflight probe may inspect Blender API and graph structure but may not render, write the formal root or emit a measurement.

sceneContract.construction: fresh factory state; analytic opaque tessellated rectangular surfaces with continuous Generated object-local emission only; no source blend, image texture, light, transparency, deformation, simulation or external asset

surfaces.localPlane: local z=0 with rectangular bounds; the independent oracle intersects all declared surfaces and chooses the nearest positive camera depth

purpose: same Object Index on two analytic owners

adapterContract.floatEncoding: little-endian finite float32 with no color transform
adapterContract.motion: vector.xy32 is current Blender Vector.XY exactly; consumer q=(x+Vector.X,y-Vector.Y); vector-next.xy32 retains current Vector.ZW for oracle validation
adapterContract.overwritePolicy: refuse if output directory or report already exists

projectionOracle.cameraConvention: Blender camera looks along local -Z; camera coordinates are transpose(R_camera_XYZ)*(world-cameraLocation)
projectionOracle.currentSurface: cast the current pixel-center ray through every declared bounded plane and select the nearest positive-depth hit; its analyticOwnerId is independent of Object Index
projectionOracle.previousSurfacePoint: inverse current owner transform maps the hit to owner-local coordinates; previous owner transform maps that same local point into world space
projectionOracle.predictedPreviousDepth: negative previous-camera Z of the transformed current local surface point
projectionOracle.independence: the analyzer implements scalar Euler XYZ, pinhole, bounded ray-plane intersection, visibility and rigid transforms without bpy, bpy_extras, mathutils or consumer imports

validWhen: the current decoded owner and depth agree with the nearest analytic current surface
all four previous bilinear taps are in bounds
current alpha and all four previous tap alphas exceed 0.999
all four previous Object Index values equal current Object Index exactly
bilinearly sampled previous Depth matches transform-predicted previous-camera depth within max(1,predictedPreviousDepth)/1024
structuralValidity.sameIndexDepthRequirement: SAME_INDEX_DEPTH_REVEAL uses equal passIndex on two analytic owners, so an owner-only rule must admit a registered wrong-history population while the depth rule rejects it
structuralValidity.invalidFallback: every structurally invalid registered current pixel copies current float32 RGBA exactly
forbidden: owner-only acceptance in the same-index fixture
global epsilon not scaled by predicted depth
reading future or target RGB to decide structural validity

candidateContract.radius2: structurally valid AND current pixel and every current neighbor within Chebyshev radius 2 share current Object Index and alpha>0.999
candidateContract.localRiskChannel: sum(abs(weight_i)*abs(previousTap_i-currentCenter)) over four bilinear taps plus one full float32 ULP at final reconstruction magnitude
candidateContract.localRiskPixel: maximum of RGB channel risks, evaluated in binary64 from float32 inputs and frozen bilinear weights
candidateContract.adaptive: radius2 AND localRiskPixel<=9.5367431640625e-7; comparison is inclusive
candidateContract.reconstruction: four-tap bilinear previous RGBA in y0x0,y0x1,y1x0,y1x1 order, float64 arithmetic and one final float32 cast
candidateContract.adaptiveFallback: registered current pixels outside adaptive copy current float32 RGBA exactly
subsetInvariants: adaptive is a subset of radius2
radius3 is a subset of radius2

comparatorContract.radius3: the same structural validity and current-neighborhood rule with Chebyshev radius 3 and no local-risk rejection
comparatorContract.frozenRationale: D12.7 showed that comparator production failure can obscure a candidate-specific result; D12.8 therefore records radius-3 quality and coverage but no radius-3 check can support, bound or reject the adaptive candidate

identity: all parent file and internal hashes match
all Blender source repeats and all canonical payload repeats are byte-identical
Python and Node reconstructed, reason, mask and risk payloads are byte-identical
the independent analyzer exactly replays every payload and decision
all required child process IDs are unique and exit zero
producer reports contain no aggregate metrics or verdicts
all registered mutation attacks are rejected

decision.supportedWhen: Every identity, projection, structural-rejection, adaptive-quality, coverage, stress, static-control, process-totality and audit-totality gate passes. Comparator measurements are excluded from this conjunction.
decision.boundedWhen: Identity, projection, structural rejection, adaptive RGB maximum/RMSE, risk conservatism, invalid fallback, process totality and audit totality pass, but any candidate coverage or risk-stress gate fails.
decision.rejectedWhen: Any identity, projection, structural-rejection, adaptive-quality, risk-conservatism, invalid-fallback, static-control, process-totality or audit-totality gate fails.
decision.comparatorExclusion: No radius-3 error, coverage or stress measurement participates in any verdict branch.
decision.noRetroactiveRelabel: D12.7 remains bounded and D12 remains not supported regardless of D12.8 outcome.

requirements: tamper a parent, runtime, tool, process or freshness identity
tamper a source EXR, array, report, typed envelope or result self-hash
flip Vector X sign, Y raster origin, pixel-center convention, Euler order or nearest-surface choice
swap analytic owners, pass indices, repeats or fixture identities
accept an out-of-bounds, wrong-owner, alpha-invalid or depth-invalid history pixel
make the same-index fixture pass with owner-only validity
alter a bilinear tap, weight, accumulation order, risk term, ULP term, channel maximum or inclusive equality
flip adaptive/radius subset or partition membership
let any comparator measurement influence verdict mapping
alter a quality, coverage, stress, static or operation-count gate

diagnostics.integrity: every diagnostic is bound to source and payload hashes but is never a measurement input

nonClaims: D12.8 does not revise the negative D12 result or the bounded D12.7 result.
D12.8 covers only opaque rigid bounded planar owners with compiler-known transforms and Object Index/depth metadata.

It does not validate curved surfaces, deformation, skinned characters, transparency, Cryptomatte fractional coverage, hair, particles, volumes, motion blur, depth of field or noisy path-traced lighting.
It does not establish temporal denoising quality, perceptual stability, cinematic quality, character consistency, production rendering or cross-platform equivalence.
A bounded result means the candidate remained numerically safe on accepted samples but rejected too much useful history or lacked preregistered stress; it is not a production promotion.
A supported result would authorize only a subsequent preregistered curved/deforming-owner experiment, not deployment.
